title: Seoul to Offer Free Bus Rides for the Elderly
paragraphs: In Seoul, older people may soon be able to ride buses for free.

In June 2026, the Seoul city council passed a new rule about free bus rides for people aged 70 and older. The vote was 69 to 1. The idea was a promise made by Seoul's mayor, Oh Se-hoon, during an election in June.

Many older people in Seoul live far from subway stations, so they use buses a lot. The plan could help these people. The free rides would be for city buses and neighborhood buses, but not for express buses.

However, the free rides will not start right away. The city still needs to decide who can get them and how many free rides they can have. According to the city, the free rides may be limited to 14 trips a month. This would cost about 52.5 billion won a year. No start date has been set yet, but the city hopes it could begin as early as next year.

At the same time, Seoul wants to make a change to free subway rides. Right now, people aged 65 and older can ride the subway for free. But the city is thinking about raising this age to 70. The free subway rides are very expensive for the city. In 2025, they caused losses of 448.8 billion won for the subway company.
Not everyone agrees with the plans. Some people worry that they will cost too much money. Some groups of older people are also against raising the age for free subway rides.
Older people are a big part of Seoul's population. People aged 65 and older make up 21.2% of the city's population.
